_about: The continents in motion, for the Time Machine (CWVault/claude/Plan-Deep-Time.md, Stage 1). pieces are present-day outlines with a plate and a lifetime in millions of years ago; plates hold each plate's finite rotation (pole lat, lon, angle in degrees) from today to each sampled age, starting at ages[first]. To draw a year: for every piece alive, take its plate's rotation at that age (slerp between samples), turn every point of its rings, project. Made by tools/plates-from-gplates.py.

source.citation: Merdith, A.S. et al. (2021), Extending full-plate tectonic models into deep time: Linking the Neoproterozoic and the Phanerozoic, Earth-Science Reviews 214, 103477
source.frame: paleomagnetic: latitude is meaningful, longitude is unconstrained before the seafloor record

howSure: see grades; positions crisp to 200 Ma, latitude only to 540, a guess beyond

units.rings: lon, lat in degrees, flat pairs
units.rot: pole lat, pole lon, angle, degrees

grades.why: the seafloor still carries its magnetic stripes, so the plates can be run backwards with confidence
rock magnetism and fossils give how far north each piece was, not how far east; the east-west positions are one best estimate
the supercontinents of this age are reconstructed from scattered evidence and the models disagree; this is one guess
